questions.answer: A little, yes. We keep a few potted plants at home, and I quite enjoy tending to them. There's something calming about [[nurturing]] something and watching it grow because of the small effort you put in.

questions.q: What kind of plants do you have at home?
questions.answer: Mostly small, [[low-maintenance]] ones on our balcony, like aloe vera, a money plant and a couple of chilli plants. My mother also grows a few herbs, which she proudly uses in her cooking.

questions.q: Does anyone in your family enjoy gardening?
questions.answer: My grandmother, without a doubt. At the village home she grows beans, pumpkins and all sorts of vegetables. Her understanding of soil and seasons is completely [[instinctive]], built up over decades rather than learned from books.

questions.q: Did you do any gardening as a child?
questions.answer: A little, at my grandparents' house. My grandfather would let me help plant seeds, and I remember checking every morning to see if anything had [[sprouted]]. That kind of patience didn't come naturally to me back then.

questions.q: Would you like to have a garden of your own one day?
questions.answer: I'd love that. Living in a flat, a proper garden isn't really possible, but in the future I'd like a small plot where I could grow vegetables. Eating something you've grown yourself must be incredibly [[rewarding]].
